title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT CONCERNING THE CONTRACTING OUT OF POST OFFICE COUNTER OPERATIONS

ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT CONCERNING THE CONTRACTING OUT OF POST OFFICE COUNTER OPERATIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) This Decree sets out the matters delegated by the Act Concerning the Contracting Out of Post Office Counter Operations and the matters necessary to implement that Act.

Article 2 (Post Office Counter Operations) The term "other operations prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 2, subparagraph 4, of the Act Concerning the Contracting Out of Post Office Counter Operations (hereinafter the "Act") means:
1. Sale of revenue stamps;
2. Operations entrusted under Article 7-2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Postal Service Act.

Article 3 (Scope of Counter Operations Eligible for Contracting Out)
(1) The Minister of Science and ICT shall determine and publicly announce the extent of post office counter operations that may be contracted out pursuant to Article 3 (1) of the Act. <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>
(2) Where the area in which the Minister intends to contract out postal savings operations under Article 3 (1) of the Act is a township (Eup) or rural district (Myeon), those operations may be contracted out only if one of the following conditions is met: <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>
1. A post office is being closed;
2. The designated area is an island or remote district identified by Ordinance of the Ministry of Science and ICT.

Article 4 (Eligibility Standards for Contracting Out Postal Savings and Insurance Operations) A person seeking to perform postal savings and postal insurance operations under contract pursuant to Article 3 (1) of the Act must satisfy every one of the following requirements: <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>
1. Have available at least one worker who will perform the contracted operations and has worked for at least five years in savings-related operations;
2. Possess facilities and related infrastructure equivalent to the facility standards for specially designated post offices under Article 3 (2) of the Special Post Offices Act;
3. Meet the additional standards determined and publicly announced by the Minister of Science and ICT for efficient performance of postal savings and insurance operations.

Article 5 (Additional Persons Eligible to Perform Contracted Post Office Counter Operations) The "persons prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 3 (2) 6 of the Act are persons satisfying at least one of the following conditions: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 21, 2013; and December 17, 2024>
1. An employer with at least 500 regularly employed workers;
2. A person who operates a chain business under Article 2, subparagraph 6, of the Distribution Industry Development Act;
3. A medical institution under Article 3 of the Medical Service Act;
4. A person who has established a pharmacy in accordance with Article 20 of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act;
5. A person with at least five years of employment at any of the following institutions:
(a) A post office under Article 27 of the Organization of Korea Post (hereinafter a "post office"), a mail-sorting center, or a logistics center;
(b) A special post office established under the Special Post Offices Act;
6. A person who has served for at least five years as a worker engaged in operations contracted out under Article 9 of the Act;
7. A person residing in a county (Gun, including the Eup and Myeon areas of a city combining urban and rural territories; the same meaning applies in this Article) who meets either of the following conditions:
(a) Has installed and maintains an individual or shared mail-receiving box under Article 43, subparagraph 4, of the Enforcement Decree of the Postal Service Act;
(b) Has entered into an agreement with a post office for the sale of postal stamps and is selling such stamps;
8. A person with at least five years of employment in the State, a local government, or a public institution under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
9. A person who has been the head of a village in a county, or who has served at least three years as a Saemaul Movement leader;
10. A person recommended by the head of the post office having jurisdiction over the area where counter operations are to be contracted out, provided that the head of that post office holds a government rank of Grade 5 or higher.

Article 6 (Publication of a Plan to Contract Out Operations) The Minister of Science and ICT must make a public announcement when intending to contract out post office counter operations under Article 3 of the Act. However, a new announcement is not required where the Minister renews an agreement for providing post office counter operations (hereinafter a "contract for outsourced operations") under Article 4 (4) of the Act, rather than entering into a new agreement under Article 4 (1). <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>

Article 7 (Selection Criteria) The criteria for selecting a person to receive a contract for outsourced operations under Article 4 (2) of the Act shall be as set forth in the attached Table.

Article 8 (Security Deposits and Related Measures)
(1) Under Article 4 (3) of the Act, the Minister of Science and ICT must require each person who enters into a contract for outsourced operations (hereinafter a "contractor") to take one of the relevant measures below, based on the scope of the operations assigned, to secure performance of that agreement: <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>
1. If only the sale of postal stamps and acceptance of postal items are contracted out:
(a) Pay the security deposit in an amount determined and publicly announced by the Minister of Science and ICT, taking into account the amount of National Treasury revenue handled and other relevant matters;
(b) Present a guarantee insurance certificate covering payment of obligations in the same amount as the deposit under item (a);
(c) Present a financial guarantee certificate securing payment of obligations in the same amount as the deposit under item (a).
2. If the operations in subparagraph 1 are contracted out together with issuing and paying postal money orders and receiving deposits and making payments through postal transfers:
(a) Pay the deposit under subparagraph 1 (a) and present the financial guarantee certificate under subparagraph 1 (c);
(b) Present the guarantee insurance certificate under subparagraph 1 (b) and the financial guarantee certificate under subparagraph 1 (c).
3. If the operations in subparagraph 2 are contracted out together with postal savings and postal insurance:
(a) Pay the deposit under subparagraph 1 (a) and present the financial guarantee certificate under subparagraph 1 (c); in this case, at least two persons must undertake joint and several liability under the financial guarantee certificate;
(b) Present the guarantee insurance certificate under subparagraph 1 (b) and the financial guarantee certificate under subparagraph 1 (c); in this case, at least two persons must undertake joint and several liability under the financial guarantee certificate.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the Minister must waive the deposit and other security measures under that paragraph for contractors covered by Article 3 (2) 1 or 2 of the Act. <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>

Article 9 (Publication of Contract Terms) Upon concluding a contract for outsourced operations, the Minister of Science and ICT must publicly announce the matters below. The same requirement applies when an agreement is terminated or its conditions are amended: <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>
1. The geographical area and designation of the operations;
2. Personal particulars of the contractor;
3. The contents of the outsourced operations;
4. The date on which the operations begin.

Article 10 (Display of Contractor Designations) When carrying out outsourced operations, a contractor must display, in a manner readily recognizable to the general public, the name of the operating area or installation site and the following designation according to the scope of the operations performed:
1. If operations under Article 2, subparagraph 1, 2 or 4, of the Act are contracted out together with operations under subparagraph 3 of that Article: "Post Office";
2. If operations under Article 2, subparagraph 1, 2 or 4, of the Act are contracted out: "Postal Service Office".

Article 11 (Training of Persons Handling Outsourced Operations)
(1) The Minister of Science and ICT may have the head of an affiliated agency or the director of the Korea Post Human Resources Development Institute train persons handling outsourced operations in accordance with the contents of the contract determined by the Minister. <Amended March 23, 2013; July 26, 2017; and December 20, 2022>
(2) Persons receiving training under paragraph (1) may be paid their actual necessary expenses within the limits of the available budget.

Article 12 (Discount Rates for Postal Stamps and Related Items) When postal stamps and related items are sold to a contractor under Article 11 (1) of the Act, the selling price shall be reduced according to the total purchase price of such items during the month concerned, using the following discount bands:
1. Up to and including 500,000 won: 15 percent;
2. The portion exceeding 500,000 won and not exceeding 1,000,000 won: 10 percent;
3. The portion exceeding 1,000,000 won and not exceeding 10,000,000 won: 5 percent;
4. The portion exceeding 10,000,000 won: 3 percent.

Article 13 (Exemption from Postage) Postage for postal items dispatched by a contractor to perform outsourced operations is exempt under Article 13 of the Act.

Article 14 (Delegation of Powers)
(1) Pursuant to Article 17 of the Act, the Minister of Science and ICT delegates the following powers to the President of Korea Post: <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>
1. Designating the areas for outsourced operations under Article 6 (1) of the Act;
2. Paying commissions for outsourced operations under Article 11 (2) of the Act;
3. Providing government goods or authorizing their free use under Article 12 of the Act;
4. Determining and announcing the scope of post office counter operations eligible for contracting out under Article 3 (1) of this Decree;
5. Determining and announcing the standards under Article 4, subparagraph 3, of this Decree;
6. Determining and announcing the amounts of security deposits under Article 8 (1);
7. Matters concerning the training of persons performing outsourced operations under Article 11.
(2) Pursuant to Article 17 of the Act, the Minister delegates the following powers to the heads of the regional postal administrations: <Amended May 30, 2011; March 23, 2013; March 27, 2017; and July 26, 2017>
1. Entering into contracts under Article 4 of the Act, including amendments to contracts; selecting contractors; and renewing the contract period;
2. Announcing plans to contract out operations under Article 6;
3. Announcing contract terms under Article 9.

Article 15 (Processing Unique Identification Information) If unavoidable for the performance of work relating to the conclusion of contracts for post office counter operations under Article 4 of the Act, the Minister of Science and ICT, including persons receiving a delegation of the Minister's powers under Article 14 (2), may process data containing resident registration numbers, passport numbers, or alien registration numbers as defined by Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act. <Amended July 26, 2017>

APPENDIX [Attached Table] — CRITERIA FOR SELECTING CONTRACTORS FOR POST OFFICE COUNTER OPERATIONS
(Related to Article 7 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act Concerning the Contracting Out of Post Office Counter Operations)
<Amended December 17, 2024>

The evaluation carries a total maximum score of 100 points. The criteria are divided into convenience of access (50 points) and ability to perform the operations (50 points).

I. CONVENIENCE OF ACCESS (50 POINTS)

A. Distance to a nearby post office (weight: 10 points)
The distance is measured as a straight line on a map. Separate assessment applies to special areas.

| Score | City area (Si) | Township or rural district (Eup/Myeon) |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | 3 km or more | 10 km or more |
| 8 | 2.5 km or more but less than 3 km | 8 km or more but less than 10 km |
| 6 | 2 km or more but less than 2.5 km | 6 km or more but less than 8 km |
| 4 | 1.5 km or more but less than 2 km | 4 km or more but less than 6 km |
| 2 | 1 km or more but less than 1.5 km | 2 km or more but less than 4 km |
| 1 | 0.5 km or more but less than 1 km | 1 km or more but less than 2 km |
| 0 | Less than 0.5 km | Less than 1 km |

B. Conditions around the proposed service location (weight: 10 points)

City area (Si):
- Mixed-use area combining office buildings, shops, and residential uses: 10 points.
- Commercial or shopping district: 8 points.
- Concentrated residential district with at least 5,000 households: 6 points.
- Within a complex of buildings: 4 points.
- Residential district: 2 points.

Township or rural district (Eup/Myeon):
- Location at the township or rural-district administrative center: 10 points.
- Residential district: 6 points.
- Other district: 2 points.

C. Transport conditions (weight: 10 points)
- Degree of adjacency to a road with at least two lanes carrying traffic in both directions: 2–4 points.
- Convenience of entry and exit, stopping, and parking for customers and mail-transport vehicles: 2–4 points.
- Ease of locating and identifying the proposed facility: 1–2 points.

D. Floor level of the proposed office (weight: 10 points)
- First floor above ground: 10 points.
- Second floor above ground: 7 points.
- First basement level: 4 points.
- Third floor above ground, if an elevator is installed: 1 point.
- Second basement level or below, and third floor above ground or higher where the specified elevator condition is not met: 0 points.

E. Ownership of the premises (weight: 5 points)
- Premises owned by the applicant: 5 points.
- Leased premises or premises owned by the applicant's family: 3 points.

F. Accessibility (weight: 5 points)
- Wheelchair access ramp installed for persons with reduced mobility: 5 points.
- Call bell installed for persons with reduced mobility: 3 points.
- No equipment or facility installed for access by persons with reduced mobility: 1 point.

II. CAPABILITY TO PERFORM THE OPERATIONS (50 POINTS)

A comprehensive assessment awarding up to 50 points, based on:
- Understanding of the postal business;
- Experience working in identical or similar public-service activities;
- Ability to provide services that satisfy customers;
- Willingness to cooperate in the development of postal business;
- Integrity, diligence, and the potential for development.

TOTAL POSSIBLE SCORE: 100 POINTS.

Note: If an applicant wishing to be entrusted with post office counter operations uses the building and facilities of a post office that has been closed, the applicant is considered to have met the requirements for the convenience-of-access category.
